subject: License model & $/1M-token targets for on-prem pilot — next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Jose Castillo <jose.castillo@acme.ai>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@acme.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: license model and $/1M-token targets for on-prem pilot

Thanks again for the call today — good to map requirements. Quick recap and asks so we can put together a clean TCO + term sheet: 

Summary (short)
- Goal: on-prem / VPC private deployment for PII-sensitive inference pipelines (customer-facing assistant + internal analytics)
- Pilot scope: 3 environments (prod, staging, dev) with a single model family; estimated steady-state token usage unknown — need your volumes
- Non-negotiables: SOC 2 evidence, customer-managed VPC, key management support

Action items we need from you to price cleanly:
1) Rough monthly token volumes (prod / staging / dev) — ballpark is fine (e.g., 100M / 10M / 5M)
2) Preferred license cadence: subscription (monthly/annual) vs term license (multi-year) vs per-environment seat? Any procurement preference?
3) Target unit economics for planning: do you have a target $/1M tokens for this deployment (or target monthly spend range)?
4) Expected concurrency / p95 latency SLOs for prod (tokens/sec or requests/sec)
5) Number of physical on-prem clusters or VPC regions that must be licensed (we discussed 1 primary + DR — confirm)

Attached: initial-pricing-scenarios.xlsx (worked examples that map license + support tier + token bands to an expected monthly ARR). I put a baseline set of unit-econ assumptions (see tab "assumptions").

Proposal for next steps from Redwood:
- You provide the ballpark numbers requested above by EOD Wed; we’ll run three modeled scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive) and return a draft term sheet + cost-per-1M-token estimates and a one-page install timeline.
- If numbers look promising, schedule a technical install scoping call with Rishi (solutions eng) to validate network/topology and sizing.

If useful, I can also pre-seed the DocuSign draft as a template for procurement (no signatures) so procurement can see line-item structure.

Thanks — diego

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0192
Attachment(s): initial-pricing-scenarios.xlsx (xlsx, 84KB); acme-soc2-ask.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: Jose Castillo <jose.castillo@acme.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@acme.ai>, procurement <procurement@acme.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: license model and $/1M-token targets for on-prem pilot

Diego — thanks for the clear recap. Per your asks, here's what we have today (ballpark):

1) Estimated monthly token volumes (starting pilot -> steady state)
- Prod: ~150M tokens / month (text gen heavy, bursts up to 10 reqs/s during daytime)
- Staging: ~20M tokens / month
- Dev: ~8M tokens / month
- Total initial: ~178M tokens/month

2) License cadence: Procurement prefers annual subscription with an option to convert to a multi-year term after pilot. They asked for clear per-env add-on pricing.

3) Budget / target economics: Finance has given a target first-year budget of $30k–$60k / month for the infra + license line (including support). They asked for a target $/1M-token metric to compare alternatives — ideally <= $350 / 1M tokens for production workloads but willing to accept higher for the pilot if we can show clear scaling benefits.

4) SLOs: p95 latency target ~600ms for short-turn assistant responses; 95% availability required for prod.

5) Environments: We will need 2 physical regions (primary + DR). For pilot we’d like 1 primary cluster and a warm-standby in a second region.

We attached the SOC2 requirements doc (acme-soc2-ask.pdf). Also attaching a simplistic network diagram (network-topology.png) — note that traffic must egress through our NAT gateway and private peering.

Next: can you run a scenario with (A) annual subscription for 1 primary + warm DR, 3 envs, 180M tokens/month and (B) same but with committed token bands (12-month) and a higher support tier (24x7)? Procurement wants to see a clear delta in unit economics and an SLA uplift cost.

Thanks — Jose

Jose Castillo
Head of Product Engineering, Acme AI
Attachment(s): acme-soc2-ask.pdf (pdf, 120KB); network-topology.png (png, 45KB)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Jose Castillo <jose.castillo@acme.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2026 12:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: license model and $/1M-token targets for on-prem pilot

Appreciate the details — that clarifies things a lot. Quick clarifications before we model: 

- When you say "committed token bands (12-month)", do you expect a hard minimum purchase each month, or a yearly committed token pool that can be consumed unevenly?
- For support tier: we’ll price Standard (business hours) vs Premium (24x7 + named CSM + 1-hr P1 response). Which does procurement prefer to see first?
- For the warm-standby DR, do you need automatic failover (active-active) or warm-passive that we can spin up within a 2-hour window?

Internal note: marissa — please prioritize scenario pricing for (A) and (B) above and include a line that converts to $/1M tokens for each band. Rishi — we’ll need a short checklist for the install call re: firewall rules, KMS endpoints, and KV cache warmup expectations (I attached network-topology.png from Acme).

I’ll return a modeled TCO PDF + draft term sheet by Wed EOD PT if we get the commit clarification.

Diego

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Jose Castillo <jose.castillo@acme.ai>, procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2026 07:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: license model and $/1M-token targets for on-prem pilot

Diego / team — looping in pricing details (high level) for the two scenarios Jose requested. See the attached spreadsheet for line-item math. Key notes in-line: 

- Scenario A (annual subscription, 1 primary + warm DR, 3 envs, no committed pool)
  - Base platform fee (annual) for Private deployment: $120k/year (covers runtime, control plane access, updates)
  - Per-env add-on: $12k/year/env -> for 3 envs = $36k/year
  - Support: Standard = included; Premium = +$48k/year
  - Token overage pricing (metered monthly): $/1M tokens = $1,200 for on-prem (no commit) — includes kernel optimizations and standard caching assumptions

- Scenario B (12-month committed token pool, annual subscription, Premium support)
  - Commit discount bands (annual commitment): 0–500M tokens: $850 / 1M; 500–1.5B: $650 / 1M; >1.5B: $500 / 1M
  - Committed-pool addendum: upfront billing for committed tokens with monthly consumption reconciliation
  - With Premium support and warm DR, expected blended cost (given 180M tokens/mo) ≈ $700 / 1M tokens (after spreading base fees and commit discount)

- Example math for Acme (180M tokens/mo) -> annualized tokens = ~2.16B tokens
  - If Acme signs a 12-mo committed contract at the 500–1.5B band, blended $/1M ≈ $650–$700; if they commit >1.5B, it moves toward $500 / 1M.

Caveats: these numbers assume the pilot can accept quantized model variants (int8/4) for a portion of inference and that KV cache reuse is enabled to reduce per-token compute. If there are strict model-accuracy constraints that deny quantization, per-1M will be ~2x of the quoted numbers.

Diego — I can convert this to a single-page pricing summary and a drill-down spreadsheet. Rishi, please add install constraints (firewall, KMS) below in thread.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa Cole
Senior Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachment(s): acme_pricing_lineitems.xlsx (xlsx, 96KB)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: Jose Castillo <jose.castillo@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: license model and $/1M-token targets for on-prem pilot

Couple of technical clarifications to bake into the install scoping and pricing assumptions:

- KV cache: For production latency targets (p95 ~600ms) we need a warmed KV cache and local SSD for large KV states. This increases node sizing for prod (~+20% GPUs) but reduces per-token cost in steady state.
- Quantization: If Acme can accept int8 quantization for up to 60% of requests (e.g., lower-risk internal analytics), that materially improves the $/1M token number.
- DR model: warm-passive (spin-up <2 hours) is cheaper and matches their ask. Active-active will double concurrency capacity and materially increase license base.
- Network: we need explicit NAT egress rules and a restricted outbound to Redwood s3 endpoints for model checksum updates. KMS must be reachable over private peering or through an approved proxy for HSM integrations.

I'll prepare a 30-min install checklist and share before the scoping call. For pricing, use the higher node sizing for prod in the first-draft TCO and mark a "node-reduction" sensitivity if cache warmup proves effective.

Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
